instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, toast the 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns in a small dry skillet over medium for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until they smell fragrant and a few pop. Tip them out, let them cool for a few minutes, then grind them as finely as you can and sift out the coarse husks.

Put the 2 tsp chili powder in a small heatproof bowl. Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in the same small skillet over medium until it shimmers, then pour it over the chili powder. It will sizzle. This is the chili oil for the table.
Mince the 5 garlic cloves and enough of the ginger to make 3 tbsp. Finely chop the 1 1/2 tbsp black beans. Thinly slice 2 of the green onions. Cut both blocks of tofu into 3/4 inch cubes.

Bring 3 cups water, the 1/2 tsp dark soy sauce and the 1/2 tsp salt to a boil in a large saucepan. Slide in the tofu, and once it's back to a boil, turn the heat down so it simmers for 3 minutes. Lift the tofu out gently with a slotted spoon into a bowl.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or large skillet over high. Add the 1/2 lb pork and break it up as it cooks until there's no pink left. Turn the heat to medium and keep cooking for 2 minutes, until it has golden, crisp bits. Stir in 1 tsp of the light soy sauce, then scoop the pork into a bowl.
Turn the heat to low and add the last 3 tbsp oil. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant but haven't browned.
Add the 1 1/2 tbsp doubanjiang and the black beans. Stir them for 3 minutes, until the oil turns red and the paste smells rich. Stir in the 1 tsp smoked paprika for 30 seconds.
Pour in the 1 cup broth and the last 1 tsp light soy sauce and turn the heat to medium high. Once it bubbles, tip in the tofu, leaving any water behind in the bowl.

Simmer it gently for 10 minutes, turning the heat down if it bubbles hard. Every few minutes, push a rubber spatula along the bottom of the pan so nothing sticks. Don't stir it, or the tofu will break up.
Meanwhile, stir the 1 tbsp cornstarch into 1/4 cup water in a small cup.

Add the 1 1/2 tsp sugar, the pork and half the ground Sichuan pepper to the pan. Pour the cornstarch mixture over the surface, then fold everything gently for about 1 minute, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Take the pan off the heat and gently stir in most of the green onions and the 1 tsp sesame oil.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Serve over the rice with the rest of the green onions on top, and the chili oil and the rest of the Sichuan pepper on the side.
method_notes: Both versions cook ground pork and garlic and ginger with doubanjiang, then warm soft or silken tofu through a thickened sauce and serve it over rice with green onion. RecipeTin Eats blanches the tofu in salted water first, fries the pork until golden, cooks fermented black beans and doubanjiang in plenty of oil, simmers the tofu in beef stock for 10 minutes and finishes with freshly ground Sichuan pepper. Just One Cookbook makes a quicker Japanese style version that adds miso, oyster sauce and mirin and warms the tofu for only a minute. This one follows RecipeTin Eats with a little more tofu and pork for a dinner for 4, and its chili powder made into a chili oil for the table so the pot stays mild.
